- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (high sentiment > 0.6) — reduce forecast by 1–3% for 30d horizon.
- Underestimate prices after sharp spikes (e.g., >75% increase in 3d) — add 2–5% buffer to forecast.
- Lagged mean reversion: if 18d history shows strong upward trend, forecast should not overshoot 30d true by >5%.
- Overshoot after sentiment reversal: if sentiment drops below 0.4 after peak, cut forecast by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.
- 30d forecasts are prone to overconfidence in early days — reduce first 5–7 days by 2–4% if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment is consistently low (<0.3) over 18d, forecast should be conservative — cap max increase at 2% per day.
- Avoid forecasting >10% above 30d true if sentiment is <0.5 — this is a high-risk overfitting signal.
